transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-15 14:30 PST · Duration 42m · Recording available
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood Solutions), Aisha (Head of Search, Onyx), Ben (ML Eng), Ravi (Platform), Claire (CTO)
Summary: discovery focused on embeddings + reranking, vector DB integration options, throughput and dimensionality tradeoffs, hybrid search with BM25 + vectors, eval plan and next steps to run benchmarks. Security questions on VPC/KMS and Private deployment.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan with Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer and Marcus on solutions. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: good thanks, excited to chat. we are re-evaluating our search stack, we've been running Elastic + some custom rerankers but latency is creeping up.
[00:15] Jordan: perfect, want to quick pull objective for today — understand current infra, scale, success criteria, and see where Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private fits right?
[00:22] Claire: yup that's right. main goals are better relevance for 90% of queries, keep P95 latency under 300ms for search path, and reduce infra cost by 20% ideally.
[00:33] Priya: great, do you mind walking through current flow and volumes?
[00:37] Ben: sure. prod traffic ~400 QPS peak, average 220 QPS. We have ~5M docs, embeddings stored in Elastic vector plugin right now, dimension 768 from our in-house embedder. Reranking is cross-encoder runs on CPU for top-50, then CPU GPU hybrid for heavy queries.
[00:55] Priya: ok got it. how's recall today, and do you rely on hybrid search (BM25 + vector) now?
[01:04] Aisha: yes hybrid, we do bm25 to candidate gen then vector similarity, recall is ok-ish but many poor long-tail queries. we think higher-dim embeddings from models like 1536 help, but worried about storage and throughput.
[01:18] Marcus: that's a common tradeoff — higher dimensionality can help separation but costs increase for vector DB storage and indexing. On Redwood we support multiple embedding dims and can serve rerankers as a second-stage cross-encoder — you can run that on Hosted for small pilots, Dedicated for production throughput, or Private if you need VPC/airgap.
[01:37] Ravi: on the security side Claire and i want to understand network controls. If we go Dedicated do we get a VPC peering and customer KMS?
[01:44] Jordan: yes Dedicated includes dedicated GPU pools, VPC peering options and KMS integration — we can bring your CMK or integrate AWS KMS/HSM. For Private we ship a customer-managed control plane option with on-prem packaging too. We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
[01:56] Claire: good. what's typical latency for a two-stage flow: vector nearest-neighbors + cross-encoder rerank? we need p95 under 300ms.
[02:04] Priya: depends on numbers. For a Hosted fast path with a 1536-dim embed and vector DB like Pinecone we typically see NN retrieval ~15-40ms (network dependent) for top-100 from a well-indexed store, and cross-encoder rerank on Dedicated GPU can do top-50 in ~60-120ms depending on model size. Combined you can hit p95 ~200-300ms if you tune batching and prefix caching.
[02:28] Ben: peg for QPS — we do bursts 400 QPS — how does Redwood handle batching and KV cache when QPS spikes?
[02:34] Priya: the serving runtime does continuous batching and KV cache. For embeddings lookup we recommend a vector DB co-located in same region; for reranker we use per-request KV cache for repeated queries and model variants. With Dedicated you can get predictable throughput and autoscaling. For Hosteds there are rate limits; we can provide burst policies for enterprise customers.
[02:52] Aisha: about vector DBs — we currently use Elastic but open to migration. what do you recommend — Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, or hosting yourself?
[03:01] Marcus: tradeoffs: Pinecone/managed DBs ease ops and provide fast ANN indexes; Weaviate/Milvus are self-hosted and better if you want full control. Redwood can integrate with any via standard API — you can also store embeddings in S3 and Redwood will index/serve if you want a managed bundle. We often recommend Pinecone or Milvus for 1M+ vectors depending on your control needs.
[03:23] Claire: budget wise — is storage per-dim charged? what's cost delta between 768 vs 1536 dims?
[03:29] Jordan: cost from vector DB side roughly linear with dimensionality for index size and ANN cost. On Redwood token costs for rerankers depend on model; embeddings generation is per-request. We'll send a matrix with example numbers but expect ~1.8-2x storage and slightly higher query latency going from 768->1536.
[03:46] Ben: on reranker models, do you support cross-encoder models on CPU? our current infra is mostly CPU, adding GPUs is heavy.
[03:53] Priya: small cross-encoders on CPU for top-10 are ok but for top-50 at 400 QPS you'll want GPU Dedicated; otherwise increase latency. Another pattern: do a cheap symmetric dot-product rerank on CPU for top-200 and cross-encoder on GPU for top-20 to balance.
[04:10] Aisha: can Redwood do hybrid search natively (bm25 + vector) or do we need to handle BM25 candidate gen in Elastic and then call Redwood?
[04:18] Marcus: Redwood focuses on model serving and rerank; candidate gen via BM25 is usually left to your search engine. That said, we have reference patterns and connectors that orchestrate BM25 candidate gen in Elastic then call Redwood for embeddings/retrieval and reranking — we can share the connector docs.
[04:33] Ravi: network flow for Dedicated — do queries route through Redwood control plane or directly to the GPU nodes? curious about egress and latencies.
[04:40] Priya: routing is policy-driven. For Dedicated with VPC peering you can have requests routed directly to infra in your region with minimal control plane hops; for Hosted they go through Redwood endpoints. We'll diagram this — lower egress and improved latency for Dedicated/Private.
[04:58] Claire: benchmark idea: we want a 1M vector test, realistic query log of 2k qps for 10 mins and tail latencies reported. Can Redwood run benchmarks or do we run against a test cluster?
[05:07] Jordan: we can help run the benchmark — Priya will own the test plan and we can run it on a Dedicated trial node or we can share the template and you run it. For accurate numbers we recommend running in your VPC or our Dedicated trial.
[05:18] Ben: about dimensionality — if we move to 1536 we need to re-embed 5M docs; time/cost estimation?
[05:24] Priya: re-embedding is embarrassingly parallel; estimate roughly X tokens per doc — we can provide throughput numbers for common models. For example, if you do batching you can embed ~10k docs/min per GPU depending on model and batching. We'll put concrete figures in the benchmark sheet.
[05:39] Aisha: any gotchas with vector index rebuilds and zero-downtime?
[05:43] Marcus: most vector DBs support index rebuilds with aliasing; pattern is build new index in background and swap alias. For self-hosted systems plan for I/O and memory. Redwood's recommended pattern has minimal service interruption.
[05:54] Claire: security — how is PII handled in hosted flows; do you purge embeddings, do you support data residency?
[06:02] Jordan: Hosted retains embeddings per your retention policy; we support customer-managed KMS for encryption and can delete embeddings on request. For strict compliance we recommend Dedicated or Private for full data residency and control.
[06:15] Aisha: do you have customers in finance/healthcare using Private?
[06:19] Jordan: yes several — we can share anonymized references and case studies.
[06:23] Priya: can i ask about eval criteria — beyond latency and cost what's the eval metric? mrr/ndcg or business KPI?
[06:30] Aisha: we use nDCG@10 and session conversion lift, also are tracking time-to-first-click.
[06:36] Priya: good — we'll map recommendations to those metrics.
[06:40] Ben: one more on blending signals — we have user signals and recency weighting, can Redwood use metadata in vector searches to bias results?
[06:48] Marcus: yes we support metadata filtering and hybrid scoring. You can do pre-filtering by metadata and also blended scoring pipelines where BM25 score, vector similarity, and recency decay are combined. We'll share patterns and config examples.
[07:05] Aisha: any limitations on embedding models? we have a custom in-house embedder.
[07:10] Priya: you can bring your own embeddings. Redwood supports storing arbitrary vector dims and will serve them; we only ask for consistent dim across a collection for indexing. If you want to use Redwood's embedder we also support several dims (384, 768, 1536).
[07:22] Claire: question on reranker cost — running cross-encoder on top-50 for 400 QPS seems expensive. any recommendations to optimize cost?
[07:29] Priya: patterns: smaller cross-encoders for top-20, asymmetric rerank where you compute cheap features + small model, caching of frequent queries, dynamic routing to cheaper model variants for non-critical users, and smart batching to amortize GPU cost. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/quantization profiles.
[07:47] Ben: what's the expected turnaround to get a Dedicated pilot up?
[07:51] Jordan: typical spinning a Dedicated trial node takes 2-5 business days once contract or trial ticket is approved; Private is longer (weeks) for on-prem packaging. For a quick pilot Hosted + Pinecone test can be same-day.
[08:02] Aisha: ok sounds good. let's recap and owners?
[08:06] Jordan: recap: Redwood to send Hosted vs Dedicated pricing and an example SOW, Priya to share benchmark template and help run 1M vector test, Onyx to provide anonymized dataset and expected QPS, schedule deep-dive for Private network design.
[08:18] Claire: thanks everyone.
[08:21] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with materials and proposed times.
[08:26] End of recording
